title: Run an incident postmortem
summary: After the incident is resolved: assemble the timeline from the incident tooling, draft the blameless write-up, hold the review, file the follow-up actions, and post the public status-page account. Setting up on-call itself lives in On-call & incidents.

parts.title: Assemble the incident timeline
parts.guidance: Build the incident timeline from alerts, deployments, logs, responder notes and support reports using one timezone. Include when users were affected, when the team noticed, what changed during mitigation and how recovery was established. Link disputed timestamps to their evidence and keep estimates visibly uncertain. Ask participants to correct gaps before analysis; keep customer identifiers and credentials out of the shared timeline.

parts.title: Draft the blameless postmortem doc
parts.guidance: Explain the incident using the timeline: user impact, detection, decisions, contributing conditions and recovery. Describe each decision in the context of the information responders had at the time. Separate a reproduced cause from a plausible hypothesis. For each proposed improvement, explain which observed failure it addresses, such as late detection or a recovery command that failed. List unresolved causal questions for the review.

parts.title: Hold the postmortem review meeting
parts.guidance: Use the review to resolve disputed timeline entries, test causal explanations and decide which improvements merit work. Bring the responders and owners needed for those questions, with the draft available beforehand. Record disagreements that remain and the actions people actually accept. Review sensitive passages before wider circulation, then update the incident account and its prioritized follow-ups.

parts.title: File follow-up actions in the tracker
parts.guidance: Turn each accepted improvement into a ticket tied to the failure it addresses. Replace vague work such as “improve alerts” with an observable result, such as a controlled failure reaching the on-call responder with the relevant diagnostic link. Use the agreed owner and priority, distinguishing proposed dates from commitments. Link tickets to the incident and keep deferred actions visible with their reason.

parts.title: Publish the status-page write-up and customer comms
parts.guidance: Write the public account from the reviewed incident facts: affected service, user-visible impact, recovery and changes customers need to know about. Reconcile times and completed fixes with the internal record; leave speculative causes and sensitive details out. Publish the incident and communications owners' authorized version to the intended channels. Check the public page and customer links, and give support the same approved account for follow-up questions.

metadata.supportReason: Timeline assembly, doc drafting, action filing, and the status-page post are API work; the blameless review is a meeting.
